title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Prop. 1 (earlier in the notes) identifies h-linear (additive, k-linear) functors F : K → B with cochain complexes C^· in B, via a universal complex 𝕀^· in K (written C^· on the page), with C_F^· = F(𝕀^·). Each object x of K is 'located' by the cochain complex of k-modules α^·(x) = Hom_K(x, 𝕀^·) in Ab_k^·. The bottom of the previous page and the top of this one define, for K^· in Ab_k^· and C^· in B^·, the object Hom^·_k(K^·, C^·) of B. It is the object representing b ↦ Hom_{B^·}(b ⊗_k K^·, C^·). In general it is the kernel of δ : ∏_i Hom_k(K^i, C^i) ⇉ ∏_i Hom_k(K^i, C^{i+1}), with δ(u) = du − ud. It exists if B has kernels, the Hom_k(K^i, C^i) are representable (e.g. K^i finitely presented), and the two products exist. That last condition is automatic if only finitely many K^i are non-zero.

Prop. 3 asserts F(x) ≅ Hom^·_k(α^·(x), F(𝕀^·)), bifunctorially in F and x. This page proves it. The map (1) F(x) → Hom^·_k(α^·(x), F(𝕀^·)) is defined by adjunction as a map of complexes (1') F(x) ⊗_k α^·(x) → F(𝕀^·). This makes sense because the α^i(x) are free of finite type. The map (1') comes from the canonical action (1'') F(x) ⊗ Hom(x, 𝕀^i) → F(𝕀^i), which is itself induced by the natural action F(x) ⊗ Hom(x, C) → F(C) for C in K.

The map (1) is natural in x, and both sides are additive in x. So it suffices to check the isomorphism for x = 𝕀^i, the components of the universal complex. Implicitly these generate K under finite sums and direct factors. For x = 𝕀^i, α^·(𝕀^i) = Hom(𝕀^i, 𝕀^·) is a representable ('free') complex. The enriched Yoneda isomorphism Hom^·_k(Hom(𝕀^i, 𝕀^·), C^·) ≅ C^i then shows that (2) F(𝕀^i) → Hom^·_k(α^·(𝕀^i), F(𝕀^·)) is the identity. QED.

In modern terms: an additive functor out of the free k-linear additive (idempotent-complete) category on a cochain complex is recovered as a weighted limit. Equivalently, it is an end/Hom of the representable weight Hom(x, 𝕀^·) into the complex F(𝕀^·). This is an enriched Yoneda/density statement. It serves the setup of the next page: the Dold–Puppe/Dold–Kan equivalences between (co)chain complexes and (co)simplicial objects in idempotent-complete additive categories, and the four canonical 'coordinate' functors α_·, α_*, α^·, α^* out of K.
errors: The reduction to x = 𝕀^i tacitly uses that K is generated by the 𝕀^i under finite direct sums and direct factors. It also needs both sides to be additive and to commute with idempotent splitting. This is presumably part of the definition of K in Prop. 1, but it is not restated here.
Existence of Hom^·_k(α^·(x), C^·) needs the products ∏_i to exist in B. The page states this only parenthetically: it is automatic if α^·(x) is bounded, which holds for x in K.

ideas.what: Reconstruction formula F(x) ≅ Hom^·_k(Hom_K(x, 𝕀^·), F(𝕀^·)) for additive functors determined by a complex.
ideas.modern_name: Enriched Yoneda lemma / weighted limit (density) formula for functors out of a free additive category on a complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Yoneda; enriched version Kelly, Day–Kelly; general category theory folklore (1960s–80s)
ideas.where_published: Yoneda-type arguments are pervasive in SGA 4 Exp. I; this specific formulation is not known to me in published Grothendieck texts

ideas.what: Definition of the internal Hom^·_k(K^·, C^·) in B as the kernel of the d-commutation map on ∏ Hom_k(K^i, C^i), with representability conditions.
ideas.modern_name: Hom complex / cotensoring of B by finite complexes of k-modules (cycles of the total Hom complex)
ideas.where_published: Similar constructions in EGA III 0 §11 and Tôhoku

ideas.what: Proof technique: check a natural transformation between additive functors on additive generators.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine enriched-Yoneda verification inside a larger construction (a universal additive category K for complexes, preparing the Dold–Puppe equivalences). The broader context of the manuscript may be of interest, but nothing on this page goes beyond standard category theory.
transcription_corrections: Top lines: probably 'produits ∏_i existent — ce qui est automatique si les K^i sont nuls sauf pour un nombre fini [d'indices]...]' rather than 'modules sur un ... fini'.
In (1), (1'), (1''): 'K^i(x)' should read α^·(x) (resp. α^i(x)); 'Hom^i_k' should be Hom^·_k; 'C^i_F' is C^·_F; 'F(C^i)' in (1), (1') is F(𝕀^·), i.e. F applied to the universal complex.
'Définissons un hom. dans \vec{B}' is more likely 'dans B' (possibly with an arrow decoration); the next line 'i.e. un hom. dans B^·' is correct.
Under (1''): 'B' and 'Ab_k' label the factors F(x) ∈ Ob B and Hom(x, 𝕀^i) ∈ Ob Ab_k (not 'Ab_K'); the word under the arrow is 'can'.
'qui provient de l'hom. fonctoriel en C ∈ Ob K'; then 'Comme (1''), donc (1) est fonctoriel en x' (the transcribed 'K' is x), and 'additifs en x', 'pour x de la forme 𝕀^i'.
Margin by (1''): 'rep. car les α^i(x) sont libres de t.f.'.
(2) should read F(𝕀^i) → Hom^·_k(𝕀^·_i, F(𝕀^·)), where 𝕀^·_i = Hom(𝕀^i, 𝕀^·); the following isomorphism is Hom^·_k(𝕀^·_i, C^·) ≃ C^i with C^· ∈ Ob B^·.
